introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Geography 2 (0550), Paper 2, ORDINARY LEVEL, JUNE 2020. Duration: Two and a Half (2 1/2) hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR Questions choosing ONE from each section.

Questions ONE carries 30 marks. All the other Questions carry 20 marks each.

Each question that is sub-divided has the sub marks in brackets.

In questions involving calculations, all steps of the working MUST be shown.

If an outline MAP and/or GRAPH are used, they must be tied inside your answer booklet, opposite the written part of the answer.

NB - ONLY THE FIRST FOUR QUESTIONS ANSWERED WILL BE MARKED.

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

(Sections: A Map Work, B Physical Geography, C Human Geography, D Cameroon Geography. Question 1 is the only question of Section A.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) On the outline map of Cameroon provided, **locate** and **name** the following:

(i) An area of grassland (ii) The northern industrial zone

(iii) An area of volcanic soils (iv) One area of dense and one area of sparse population.

![fig-1](gce-ol-geography-2020-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The outline shows only the border of Cameroon with the north arrow (southern border at about 2 degrees N, Atlantic coast in the south-west, Lake Chad at about 13 degrees N). Mark each feature and write its name beside it.

**(i) An area of grassland:** the **Adamawa Plateau** in the centre (about 6 to 8 degrees N), or the **Western Highlands grassfields** (Bamenda grassfields), or the **northern savanna plains** (Benoue plains).

**(ii) The northern industrial zone:** the area around **Garoua** (with **Maroua** and **Ngaoundere**), in the north, at about 9 degrees N on the River Benue: cotton ginning, textiles, food processing and breweries.

**(iii) An area of volcanic soils:** the slopes of **Mount Cameroon** (around Buea and Limbe, in the south-west, at about 4 degrees N); also the **Western Highlands** (Bamenda and Bafoussam areas, Mount Manengouba), where the soils are fertile.

**(iv) Population:** one **dense** area, for example the **Western Highlands** (Bamenda-Bafoussam) or the **Douala coastal area**; one **sparse** area, for example the **East Region** (south-east forest).

questions.enonce_markdown:
(b) Describe **THREE** ways by which the primary resources of Cameroon are being developed for economic emergence.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
The government's aim is for Cameroon to become an **emerging economy** (the long-term plan is called Vision 2035). **Primary resources** (crops, forests, minerals, oil and water) are being developed in the following ways:

1. **Modernising agriculture and processing farm products.** Large agro-industrial plantations (such as those of the Cameroon Development Corporation, with rubber, oil palm, banana and tea) and cooperatives are supported; the government encourages farmers to use improved seeds and fertilisers and to process products such as cocoa, cotton and sugar cane locally before export.
2. **Managing forests and encouraging local timber processing.** Forest concessions are given under management plans, and sawmills and factories (plywood, veneer, furniture) are encouraged, so that more timber is exported as manufactured goods rather than as raw logs.
3. **Developing minerals, oil and energy.** Oil is produced offshore and exported (the Chad-Cameroon pipeline reaches the Atlantic coast at Kribi), and mining of iron ore, bauxite, cobalt, gold and limestone is being developed through licences to companies. Dams and gas plants (such as Lom Pangar and the Kribi gas plant) increase electric power for industry.

Each of these helps by creating **jobs, earning foreign exchange and supplying raw materials to industries**.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(c) Explain **THREE** problems faced by urban areas in Cameroon.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Cameroon's towns (especially Douala and Yaounde) are growing very fast because of rural-urban migration and a high birth rate, which causes problems.

1. **Housing shortage and slums.** Houses are too few and too costly, so many people live in overcrowded and badly built houses in spontaneous settlements without roads, water and electricity, often on swampy or steep land which floods or slips.
2. **Traffic congestion.** Narrow, poorly maintained roads and too many vehicles and motorcycle taxis cause long traffic jams, delays and accidents, especially at peak hours.
3. **Poor sanitation, waste and flooding.** Refuse collection and drains do not keep pace with the population, so waste piles up and blocks gutters. This causes floods in the rainy season, pollution and diseases such as cholera and malaria.

Other problems that may be given: **unemployment and underemployment** (many people work in the informal sector), **crime**, and shortages of water, electricity and schools.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(d) Suggest how the transport sector of Cameroon can be made more efficient.

(3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. **Build, tar and maintain roads**, especially the roads linking the regions and neighbouring countries, and modernise the Douala-Yaounde link (a motorway project).
2. **Modernise and extend the railway** (Camrail) and improve the ports (Douala and the new Kribi deep-sea port) and airports to move goods and people quickly and cheaply.
3. **Improve traffic management and public transport in the towns** (buses, better traffic control, strict enforcement of road and axle-load rules) to reduce accidents and delays.
